question: The parliamentary standing committees have a tenure of ________ years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is one.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's Parliamentary Standing Committees are permanent (constituted every year or periodically) committees of Parliament that examine bills, budgets (Demands for Grants) and the working of ministries. (संसदीय स्थायी समिति — एक वर्ष का कार्यकाल)

 

• The 24 Department-Related Standing Committees (DRSCs) — 16 under Lok Sabha and 8 under Rajya Sabha — are reconstituted every year, giving each committee and its members a tenure of one year.

 

• Standing Committees are distinct from ad hoc committees (like Select/Joint Committees), which are formed for a specific purpose and dissolved once that purpose is fulfilled.

 

• The Standing Committee system in its present form was introduced in 1993 to enable detailed scrutiny of legislation and government spending away from the floor of the House.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chairman of a DRSC is appointed by the Speaker (Lok Sabha committees) or the Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Rajya Sabha committees) from among the members.

 

• Besides DRSCs, Parliament also has Financial Committees (Public Accounts Committee, Estimates Committee, Committee on Public Undertakings), which also generally function with a one-year term for their composition.

 

NOTE

 

• Four years / Three years / Two years (Options 2, 3 and 4): None of these match the actual one-year reconstitution cycle of the standing committees; they are incorrect distractors.

question: Which military officer led the British forces in the Battle of Chinhat fought in 1857?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Henry Lawrence.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Battle of Chinhat was fought on 30 June 1857 near Lucknow during the Revolt of 1857, between British forces and the rebel sepoys/Awadh forces. (चिनहट का युद्ध — हेनरी लॉरेंस)

 

• The British forces were led by Sir Henry Montgomery Lawrence, the Chief Commissioner of Awadh, who was persuaded against his own judgement to march out and confront the much larger rebel force.

 

• The British contingent was decisively defeated, forcing Lawrence to retreat into the Residency at Lucknow, which was then besieged for several months (the Siege of Lucknow).

 

• Henry Lawrence was mortally wounded by a shell during the siege and died on 4 July 1857, shortly after the battle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• After Lawrence's death, the defence of the Lucknow Residency was carried on under Brigadier John Inglis and later relieved by forces under Henry Havelock, James Outram, and finally Colin Campbell.

 

• The Revolt of 1857 in Awadh was strongly linked to the annexation of Awadh in 1856 by Lord Dalhousie under the Doctrine of Lapse-related policies.

 

NOTE

 

• Robert Maclagan (Option 1): A Royal Engineers officer of the period, not the commander at Chinhat.

 

• James George Smith (Option 3): Not associated with commanding the British force at the Battle of Chinhat.

 

• Charles Ellice (Option 4): A British officer of the era, but not the officer who led the British force at Chinhat.

question: Citizens are NOT discriminated against on the basis of religion, caste or sex because of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right to Equality.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Right to Equality (Articles 14-18 of the Indian Constitution) guarantees that the State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth. (समानता का अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 14-18)

 

• Article 14 guarantees equality before law and equal protection of laws to all persons.

 

• Article 15 specifically prohibits discrimination by the State against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth, and also bars restrictions on access to shops, public restaurants, wells, roads etc. on these grounds.

 

• Article 16 extends the principle of equality of opportunity to matters of public employment, and Article 17 abolishes untouchability.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 18 abolishes titles (other than military/academic distinctions), preventing the creation of a privileged class.

 

• The Right to Equality is one of the six Fundamental Rights guaranteed under Part III of the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Right against Exploitation (Option 2): Articles 23-24; prohibits human trafficking, forced labour, and child labour in hazardous employment.

 

• Right to Freedom (Option 3): Articles 19-22; guarantees freedoms of speech, assembly, movement, profession, etc., and protection of life and personal liberty.

 

• Right to Freedom of Religion (Option 4): Articles 25-28; guarantees freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion, not specifically non-discrimination.

question: Which is the nearest planet to the Sun?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mercury.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mercury is the smallest and innermost planet of the Solar System, orbiting the Sun at an average distance of about 58 million km. (बुध ग्रह — सूर्य के सबसे निकट)

 

• Its close proximity gives it the shortest orbital period of all planets — about 88 Earth days to complete one revolution around the Sun.

 

• Mercury has no significant atmosphere, which causes extreme temperature variation between its day side (up to ~430°C) and night side (as low as ~-180°C).

 

• The order of planets by distance from the Sun is: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mercury has been explored by NASA's Mariner 10 and MESSENGER missions, and is currently being studied by the joint ESA-JAXA BepiColombo mission.

 

• Venus, though farther from the Sun than Mercury, is the hottest planet due to its thick, heat-trapping CO₂ atmosphere.

 

NOTE

 

• Uranus (Option 1): The seventh planet from the Sun, an ice giant known for its extreme axial tilt.

 

• Jupiter (Option 2): The fifth planet from the Sun and the largest planet in the Solar System.

 

• Saturn (Option 4): The sixth planet from the Sun, famous for its prominent ring system.

question: Name the Chola inscription that provided details of the way in which the sabha was organised in the local administration in the Chola empire.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttaramerur inscription.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Uttaramerur inscriptions, found in Uttaramerur village (Kanchipuram district, Tamil Nadu), belong to the reign of the Chola king Parantaka I (10th century CE). (उत्तरमेरूर अभिलेख — चोल सभा प्रशासन)

 

• They describe in remarkable detail the constitution of the local sabha (village assembly of Brahmadeya/agrahara villages) — eligibility criteria for membership, the process of selection by lot (kudavolai system), tenure, and the various sub-committees (variyams) such as the tank committee and garden committee.

 

• These inscriptions are considered one of the most important sources for understanding local self-government in early medieval South India.

 

• The Chola local administrative units were structured as Mandalam (province) → Valanadu → Nadu → Kurram/village, with the ur (assembly of non-Brahmadeya villages) and sabha/mahasabha (assembly of Brahmadeya villages) forming the base of rural administration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Thiruvalangadu inscription (also of Chola origin) is significant chiefly for tracing the Chola dynastic genealogy and describing Rajaraja I's conquests, not the sabha's constitution.

 

• The kudavolai (pot-and-ticket) system used to select sabha members by lot at Uttaramerur is often cited as an early example of grassroots democratic practice in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Thiruvalangadu inscription (Option 1): Primarily a genealogical record of the Chola dynasty, not about sabha organisation.

 

• Thirunanthikarai inscription (Option 2): Not the record associated with the sabha's constitution.

 

• Darsanam Koppu inscription (Option 3): Not the record associated with the sabha's constitution.

question: Since 1994, Winter Olympics traditionally take place _____ after the Summer Olympics.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2 years.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Until 1992, the Summer and Winter Olympics were held in the same calendar year, every four years. (शीतकालीन ओलंपिक — ग्रीष्मकालीन के 2 वर्ष बाद)

 

• From 1994 onward, the International Olympic Committee staggered the two Games, so that the Winter Olympics now falls two years after the preceding Summer Olympics (and two years before the next one).

 

• The last Winter Games held in the same year as a Summer Games was 1992 (Albertville); the next Winter Games, Lillehammer 1994, began the new staggered 2-year cycle.

 

• Both Summer and Winter Olympics are still held every four years each, just offset from one another by two years, e.g., Summer 2024 (Paris) → Winter 2026 (Milano Cortina).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The staggering was intended to give better commercial and broadcasting focus to each Games individually, rather than having both compete for attention in the same year.

 

• The International Olympic Committee (IOC) is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.

 

NOTE

 

• 4 years (Option 1): This is the interval between successive editions of the same Games (Summer-to-Summer or Winter-to-Winter), not between a Summer Games and the following Winter Games.

 

• 3 months / 6 months (Options 2 and 3): Both are far too short; the actual gap introduced since 1994 is two years.

question:
Which of the following statement/s about the Green Revolution is/are CORRECT?

i. India became self-sufficient with the introduction of the Green Revolution.

ii. The Green Revolution led to loss of nutrients in the soil from farming the same crop over and over again.

iii. The Green Revolution led to depletion of fresh ground water.
solution_text:
The correct answer is i, ii and iii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Green Revolution, introduced in India in the mid-1960s under the guidance of Dr. M. S. Swaminathan (with high-yielding variety seeds developed in part by Norman Borlaug), transformed India from a food-deficit to a largely food self-sufficient nation, especially in wheat and rice. (हरित क्रांति — खाद्यान्न आत्मनिर्भरता एवं पर्यावरणीय प्रभाव)

 

• Statement i is correct: Through high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, irrigation and mechanisation, India moved away from being dependent on food imports (like the PL-480 wheat imports from the US) towards self-sufficiency in foodgrain production.

 

• Statement ii is correct: The Green Revolution's emphasis on monocropping (repeatedly growing the same high-yield crop, e.g., wheat-rice rotation) along with heavy chemical fertilizer use led to depletion of soil micronutrients and declining soil fertility over time.

 

• Statement iii is correct: The intensive irrigation required by HYV crops, especially in Punjab and Haryana, led to over-extraction of groundwater, causing a significant and continuing decline in the water table in these regions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution was concentrated mainly in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, and mainly benefited wheat and rice, leading to regional and crop-wise imbalances.

 

• Criticisms of the Green Revolution also include increased income inequality among farmers (large farmers benefiting more than small/marginal ones) and greater pesticide/fertilizer pollution.

 

NOTE

 

• Only i and iii (Option 2): Incorrectly excludes statement ii, which is also a well-documented consequence (soil nutrient loss from monocropping).

 

• Only i and ii (Option 3): Incorrectly excludes statement iii, which is also a well-documented consequence (groundwater depletion).

 

• Only ii (Option 4): Incorrectly excludes statements i and iii, both of which are also correct.

question: What was the Child Sex Ratio in the country as per the Census of India 2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 919.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, the Child Sex Ratio (CSR), defined as the number of females per 1000 males in the 0-6 years age group, stood at 919. (बाल लिंगानुपात 2011 — 919)

 

• This represented a decline from the 2001 Census figure of 927, indicating a worsening of the child sex ratio over that decade despite the overall (all-age) sex ratio improving.

 

• The overall sex ratio of India as per Census 2011 was 943 females per 1000 males, distinct from and higher than the child sex ratio.

 

• The decline in CSR has been attributed largely to female foeticide and sex-selective practices, prompting government schemes such as Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (launched 2015).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per Census 2011, Haryana recorded one of the lowest child sex ratios among states, while states like Mizoram recorded comparatively favourable ratios.

 

• Census 2011 was India's 15th Census and the 7th after independence, conducted under the slogan "Our Census, Our Future".

 

NOTE

 

• 189 (Option 1): Not a real figure for any national sex-ratio statistic; a distractor formed by digit rearrangement of 919.

 

• 911 (Option 2): Not the correct 2011 figure for the child sex ratio.

 

• 981 (Option 3): Not the correct 2011 figure for the child sex ratio.

question: As per Census of India 2011, in which of the following states was the total population less than 10 lakh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sikkim.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, Sikkim had a total population of approximately 6.1 lakh (610,577), making it the least populous state in India and the only one among the given options with a population below 10 lakh. (सिक्किम — जनसंख्या 10 लाख से कम)

 

• Goa's 2011 population was about 14.6 lakh (1,458,545), and Tripura's was about 36.7 lakh (3,673,917) — both above 10 lakh.

 

• Telangana was carved out as a separate state only in 2014; the region's population as enumerated in the composite Andhra Pradesh in the 2011 Census was far above 10 lakh (in the crores).

 

• Sikkim is also the least populous state of India in the 2011 Census overall, ahead even of Union Territories in some comparisons.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Among Union Territories, Lakshadweep has the smallest population (about 64,000 as per 2011 Census), smaller than any full state including Sikkim.

 

• Uttar Pradesh was the most populous state in the 2011 Census, with over 19.9 crore people.

 

NOTE

 

• Telangana (Option 1): Did not exist as a separate state at the time of the 2011 Census; its constituent districts had a combined population well above 10 lakh.

 

• Goa (Option 3): Had a 2011 population of about 14.6 lakh, above the 10 lakh threshold.

 

• Tripura (Option 4): Had a 2011 population of about 36.7 lakh, well above the 10 lakh threshold.

question: In MS-Word, a document may be printed using ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ctrl+P.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Microsoft Word (and most other applications following Windows conventions), the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+P opens the Print dialog/Print backstage view, allowing a document to be printed. (Ctrl+P — मुद्रण/प्रिंट शॉर्टकट)

 

• Ctrl+X is the shortcut for Cut — it removes the selected content and places it on the clipboard.

 

• Ctrl+C is the shortcut for Copy — it copies the selected content to the clipboard without removing it.

 

• Ctrl+V is the shortcut for Paste — it inserts the clipboard's content at the cursor position.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common MS-Word shortcuts include Ctrl+S (Save), Ctrl+Z (Undo), Ctrl+Y (Redo), Ctrl+B (Bold), Ctrl+I (Italic), and Ctrl+U (Underline).

 

• Ctrl+P is a near-universal print shortcut across most Windows applications, including web browsers.

 

NOTE

 

• Ctrl+X (Option 1): Cuts the selected text/object, not related to printing.

 

• Ctrl+C (Option 2): Copies the selected text/object, not related to printing.

 

• Ctrl+V (Option 4): Pastes previously copied/cut content, not related to printing.

question: Which of the following Articles was amended in the Constitution (Fifth Amendment Act), 1955?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constitution (Fifth Amendment) Act, 1955 amended Article 3 of the Constitution of India. (पांचवां संविधान संशोधन 1955 — अनुच्छेद 3)

 

• Article 3 deals with the formation of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries or names of existing states by Parliament.

 

• Before this amendment, the President was required to refer a state-reorganisation Bill to the affected State Legislature and had to wait for the period specified for the Legislature to express its views before introducing the Bill in Parliament.

 

• The Fifth Amendment empowered the President to fix the time period within which the State Legislature must give its views on such a Bill, and clarified that Parliament could proceed even without receiving that opinion within the specified time — streamlining the process of state reorganisation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The States Reorganisation Act, 1956, which reorganised Indian states largely on linguistic lines, was enacted using the enhanced procedure enabled under the amended Article 3.

 

• Article 3 also allows Parliament to increase or diminish the area of any state and to alter its boundaries or name, by a simple majority (not a constitutional amendment) under the ordinary legislative process, though the Fifth Amendment itself was passed via the amendment procedure under Article 368.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 45 (Option 1): A Directive Principle relating to (originally) free and compulsory education for children; not touched by the Fifth Amendment.

 

• Article 34 (Option 3): Relates to restriction on rights during martial law; not the subject of the Fifth Amendment.

 

• Article 17 (Option 4): Abolishes untouchability; not related to the Fifth Amendment.

question: Which of the following is a string instrument commonly featured in the folk music of Gujarat?
solution_text:
The correct answer is jantar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gujarati folk music employs a range of traditional instruments across wind, string and percussion categories, and the jantar is one of the notable string instruments used, especially among the state's tribal communities. (जंतर — गुजराती लोक संगीत का तार वाद्य)

 

• Turi, pava and bungal are all wind (blown) instruments traditionally used in Gujarati folk music, often played during festivals, weddings and tribal dances.

 

• Other string instruments of Gujarati folk tradition include the ravan hattho and the ektaro, often accompanying folk songs and Garba/Raas performances.

 

• Percussion instruments commonly used include the manjira and the zanz (a pot drum).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ravan hattho is a bowed string instrument, believed to be one of the earliest ancestors of the modern violin, traditionally played by folk balladeers of Gujarat and Rajasthan.

 

• Gujarati folk dances such as Garba and Raas are traditionally accompanied by a mix of these string, wind and percussion instruments along with singing.

 

NOTE

 

• Turi (Option 1): A wind instrument, not a string instrument.

 

• Bungal (Option 2): A wind instrument, not a string instrument.

 

• Pava (Option 4): A wind instrument (a type of flute), not a string instrument.

question:
A housemaid gets her 12-year-old daughter to help in her work as a house cleaner at a residential colony instead of sending her to school.

Which fundamental duty is violated by the housemaid?
option_1: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
option_2: To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood
option_3: To defend the country and render national service
option_4: To provide opportunities for education to his/her child
solution_text:
The correct answer is To provide opportunities for education to his/her child.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 51A(k) of the Indian Constitution, inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, it is a Fundamental Duty of every parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child (or, as the case may be, ward) between the ages of 6 and 14 years. (मौलिक कर्तव्य अनुच्छेद 51A(k) — शिक्षा का अवसर प्रदान करना)

 

• By making her 12-year-old daughter work as a house cleaner instead of sending her to school, the housemaid is directly denying her child's right/opportunity to education, violating this specific fundamental duty.

 

• This duty was added alongside the Right to Education (Article 21A), which made free and compulsory education a fundamental right for children in the 6-14 age group.

 

• The Fundamental Duties, listed under Article 51A (Part IVA of the Constitution), were originally added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties listed in Article 51A, applicable to all citizens of India (not enforceable by courts, but morally and constitutionally significant).

 

• The scenario in this question could also raise child-labour law concerns (e.g., under the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act), but the fundamental-duty angle specifically concerns Article 51A(k).

 

NOTE

 

• To safeguard public property and to abjure violence (Option 1): Article 51A(i); unrelated to denying a child education.

 

• To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood (Option 2): Article 51A(e); concerns communal harmony, not education.

 

• To defend the country and render national service (Option 3): Article 51A(d); concerns national defence, not education.

question: Which of the following types of music is confined to the states of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carnatic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Carnatic music is one of the two principal traditions of Indian classical music, prevalent mainly in the southern states — Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh (and Telangana), Tamil Nadu and Kerala. (कर्नाटक संगीत — दक्षिण भारत)

 

• It is characterised by compositions (kritis) that are largely devotional, built around fixed melodic frameworks called ragas and rhythmic cycles called talas, with the veena, violin, mridangam and flute as prominent accompanying instruments.

 

• Renowned composers of Carnatic music, collectively called the "Trinity of Carnatic music", are Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri.

 

• Hindustani classical music, by contrast, developed mainly in North India and shows influences of Persian and Central Asian musical traditions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Famous Carnatic vocalists/instrumentalists include M.S. Subbulakshmi, Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer, and violinist Lalgudi Jayaraman.

 

• Both Carnatic and Hindustani music are branches of India's broader classical music tradition, which itself is a wider term (Option 1) not confined to only these four southern states.

 

NOTE

 

• Classical (Option 1): Too broad a term — includes both Carnatic (South) and Hindustani (North) traditions, not confined to the four southern states alone.

 

• Regional (Option 3): A generic term for folk/local music forms, not a formal music system confined specifically to these four states.

 

• Hindustani (Option 4): Predominant in North India, not the four southern states mentioned.

question: How can you access the Step by Step Mail Merge Wizard in Microsoft Word?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Clicking on the Mailings tab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Microsoft Word, the Step by Step Mail Merge Wizard is accessed via the Mailings tab on the Ribbon, by clicking Start Mail Merge → Step-by-Step Mail Merge Wizard. (मेल मर्ज विज़ार्ड — Mailings टैब)

 

• The Mail Merge Wizard guides the user through creating personalised documents (letters, envelopes, labels, emails) by combining a main document with a data source (such as an Excel sheet or Word/Access table of names and addresses).

 

• The wizard walks through six steps: selecting the document type, starting document, recipients, writing the letter, previewing letters, and completing the merge.

 

• Ctrl+M in Word is generally used to indent a paragraph, not to open Mail Merge; F12 opens the Save As dialog.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Mailings tab in MS Word also includes options like Insert Merge Field, Preview Results, and Finish & Merge, all used as part of the mail-merge process.

 

• Mail Merge is commonly used to generate bulk, personalised documents such as invitation letters, admit cards, or address labels.

 

NOTE

 

• Clicking on the File menu (Option 1): The File menu provides options like New, Open, Save, Print — not the Mail Merge Wizard directly.

 

• Pressing Ctrl + M (Option 2): This shortcut indents a paragraph in Word, not related to Mail Merge.

 

• Pressing F12 (Option 4): This shortcut opens the Save As dialog box, not the Mail Merge Wizard.

question: Which of the following is a medium-sized globular protein that acts as a pancreatic serine protease found in the digestive system of many vertebrates?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Trypsin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Trypsin is a medium-sized globular protein and a serine protease enzyme secreted by the pancreas (initially as inactive trypsinogen) into the small intestine, where it helps digest proteins. (ट्रिप्सिन — अग्न्याशय का सेरीन प्रोटीज़)

 

• Trypsin works by cleaving peptide bonds on the carboxyl side of the amino acids lysine and arginine, breaking down dietary proteins into smaller peptides.

 

• It is activated from its zymogen (inactive) form trypsinogen by the enzyme enterokinase (enteropeptidase) present in the duodenal (small intestine) lining.

 

• Being a serine protease, trypsin's active site contains a catalytically crucial serine residue involved in the hydrolysis of peptide bonds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other pancreatic digestive enzymes include chymotrypsin (another serine protease), pancreatic amylase (digests starch), and pancreatic lipase (digests fats).

 

• Pepsin, unlike trypsin, is a protease secreted by the stomach and works optimally in a highly acidic environment.

 

NOTE

 

• Amylase (Option 1): A carbohydrate-digesting enzyme (breaks down starch into sugars), not a protease.

 

• Lipase (Option 2): A fat-digesting enzyme (breaks down triglycerides), not a protease.

 

• Pepsin (Option 4): A protease, but secreted in the stomach, not the pancreas, and is not classified as trypsin.

question: Buddh International Circuit is located at:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Noida.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Buddh International Circuit is a motorsport race track located in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, in the National Capital Region. (बुद्ध इंटरनेशनल सर्किट — नोएडा)

 

• It was built by the Jaypee Group and hosted the Indian Grand Prix (Formula 1) in 2011, 2012 and 2013.

 

• The circuit was designed by renowned track architect Hermann Tilke, who has also designed several other F1 circuits worldwide.

 

• It has a track length of about 5.14 km and was India's first purpose-built Formula 1 circuit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The circuit has also hosted MotoGP (Indian Grand Prix) motorcycle races and other motorsport events in recent years.

 

• India's Formula 1 race (Indian Grand Prix) was discontinued after 2013 due to tax and financial disputes.

 

NOTE

 

• Chennai (Option 1): Not the location of the Buddh International Circuit.

 

• Mumbai (Option 3): Not the location of the Buddh International Circuit.

 

• Delhi (Option 4): The circuit is often loosely associated with the Delhi-NCR region in casual usage, but it is actually located in Greater Noida (Uttar Pradesh), not within Delhi itself.

question: The Supreme Court, in May 2023, observed that it can give divorce on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage by exercising its discretionary power under ________.
option_1: Article 136 of the Constitution of India
option_2: Article 32 of the Constitution of India
option_3: Article 142 of the Constitution of India
option_4: Article 143 of the Constitution of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 142 of the Constitution of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In May 2023, in the case of Shilpa Sailesh v. Varun Sreenivasan, a five-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court held that it can grant divorce on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage by directly exercising its discretionary power under Article 142, without referring the couple to a Family Court. (अनुच्छेद 142 — सर्वोच्च न्यायालय का विवेकाधीन अधिकार)

 

• Article 142 empowers the Supreme Court to pass any decree or order necessary for doing "complete justice" in any matter pending before it, and such an order is enforceable throughout India.

 

• The Court clarified that this discretion must be exercised carefully, examining factors such as the duration of separation, failed attempts at reconciliation, and children's welfare, before dissolving a marriage on this ground.

 

• This ruling is significant because irretrievable breakdown of marriage is not a statutory ground for divorce under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955; the Supreme Court's Article 142 power effectively fills this legislative gap.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 142 has also been invoked in other landmark matters, such as the Ayodhya land dispute verdict (2019), to ensure equitable resolution.

 

• The Law Commission of India (in its 71st Report, 1978) had earlier recommended adding irretrievable breakdown as a statutory ground for divorce, a reform still pending in legislation.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 136 (Option 1): Grants the Supreme Court special leave to appeal against judgments/orders of any court or tribunal, not the power used here.

 

• Article 32 (Option 2): Grants citizens the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights via writs, not the basis of this ruling.

 

• Article 143 (Option 4): Empowers the President to seek the Supreme Court's advisory opinion, not relevant to this divorce ruling.

question: What is known to be 'ekaharya', where one dancer takes on many roles in a single performance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bharatanatyam, one of the oldest classical dance forms of India originating in Tamil Nadu, is traditionally performed as a solo (ekaharya) dance, in which a single dancer portrays multiple characters/roles within one performance through changes in expression, gesture and posture. (एकाहार्य — भरतनाट्यम की एकल शैली)

 

• The term "ekaharya" (literally, one person carrying/representing many) reflects this solo performance tradition, rooted in the Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni, the foundational treatise on Indian performing arts.

 

• In a Bharatanatyam recital, the dancer uses precise mudras (hand gestures), abhinaya (expressive acting) and footwork to shift seamlessly between different characters and narrative viewpoints without changing costume.

 

• Bharatanatyam typically follows a structured recital format called margam, including items like Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam, Padam, and Tillana.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bharatanatyam is traditionally accompanied by Carnatic music, with a nattuvanar conducting the rhythm through cymbals (nattuvangam).

 

• Legendary Bharatanatyam exponents include Rukmini Devi Arundale, who played a key role in reviving and popularising the form in the 20th century.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathak (Option 2): A North Indian classical dance form known for its spins (chakkars) and storytelling through Persian-influenced elements; not specifically termed "ekaharya".

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 3): A classical dance-drama form of Andhra Pradesh, traditionally performed by a group/troupe rather than as a strict solo "ekaharya" tradition.

 

• Kathakali (Option 4): A dance-drama of Kerala performed by multiple dancers, each representing a different character with elaborate makeup and costume, the opposite of one dancer playing many roles.

question:
Match the railway zones in column A with their headquarters in column B.

Column A (Railway zones): 1. Central  2. Northern  3. Eastern  4. Southern

Column B (Headquarters): a. New Delhi  b. Mumbai CST  c. Chennai  d. Kolkata
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-b, 2-a, 3-d, 4-c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indian Railways is divided into multiple zones, each with its own headquarters, for administrative and operational efficiency. (भारतीय रेलवे क्षेत्र — मुख्यालय)

 

• Central Railway zone's headquarters is at Mumbai CST (Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus) — matches 1-b.

 

• Northern Railway zone's headquarters is at New Delhi — matches 2-a.

 

• Eastern Railway zone's headquarters is at Kolkata — matches 3-d.

 

• Southern Railway zone's headquarters is at Chennai — matches 4-c.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Central Railway was one of the original zones formed in 1951, and Mumbai CST is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

• Other major zones include Western Railway (Mumbai Churchgate), South Central Railway (Secunderabad), North Eastern Railway (Gorakhpur), and South Eastern Railway (Kolkata/Garden Reach).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 each mismatch at least one zone-headquarters pairing (e.g., swapping Northern/Eastern or Eastern/Southern headquarters), which is factually incorrect based on the actual Indian Railways zonal headquarters.

question: The central stretch of the Western Coastal Plains of India is known as the:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kannad plains.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Western Coastal Plains of India, stretching from Gujarat to Kerala along the Arabian Sea, are conventionally divided into three sections from north to south. (पश्चिमी तटीय मैदान — तीन भाग)

 

• The northern stretch (Maharashtra-Goa) is called the Konkan coast; the central stretch, running along Karnataka, is called the Kannada/Kanara coast (Kannad plains); and the southern stretch (Kerala) is called the Malabar coast.

 

• The Kannad (Kanara) coast lies between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea along Karnataka, and is generally narrower than the Malabar coast to its south.

 

• The Malabar coast (Kerala) is distinctive for its lagoons and backwaters (kayals), such as the famous Vembanad Lake.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Eastern Coastal Plains, by contrast, are divided into the Utkal Plain (Odisha), Andhra Plain, and Coromandel Coast (Tamil Nadu).

 

• The Western Coastal Plains are generally narrower than the Eastern Coastal Plains because the Western Ghats lie much closer to the Arabian Sea coast than the Eastern Ghats do to the Bay of Bengal coast.

 

NOTE

 

• Konkan coast (Option 1): This is the northern stretch of the Western Coastal Plains (Maharashtra-Goa), not the central stretch.

 

• Coromandel coast (Option 2): This is part of the Eastern Coastal Plains (Tamil Nadu-Andhra), not the Western Coastal Plains at all.

 

• Malabar coast (Option 3): This is the southern stretch of the Western Coastal Plains (Kerala), not the central stretch.

question: The Kutch festival is held at ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhuj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kutch (Kachchh) Festival, also popularly known as "Rann Utsav", is held in and around Bhuj, the district headquarters of Kutch district, Gujarat, with its famous venue at Dhordo village near the White Rann (Rann of Kutch). (कच्छ महोत्सव / रण उत्सव — भुज)

 

• The festival typically runs from around November to February, showcasing the region's handicrafts, folk music, folk dance, cuisine, and the stark white salt desert of the Great Rann of Kutch.

 

• It has become a major tourism initiative of the Gujarat Tourism department, attracting both domestic and international visitors to experience Kutch's unique culture and landscape.

 

• Dhordo, the tented city hub of the Rann Utsav, was recognised as the "Best Tourism Village" by the UN World Tourism Organization (UNWTO) in 2023.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Great Rann of Kutch is one of the largest salt deserts in the world, famous for its full-moon night views of the white salt flats.

 

• Gujarat also hosts other notable cultural events like the International Kite Festival (Ahmedabad) and Navratri Garba celebrations across the state.

 

NOTE

 

• Surat (Option 1): A major city of Gujarat known for diamonds and textiles, not the venue of the Kutch Festival.

 

• Rajkot (Option 2): A major city in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, not the venue of the Kutch Festival.

 

• Ahmedabad (Option 4): Gujarat's largest city and host of other festivals like the Kite Festival, but not the Kutch Festival.

question: What is the use of Net National Product (NNP)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is To calculate per capita income.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Net National Product (NNP) is obtained by subtracting depreciation (consumption of fixed capital) from Gross National Product (GNP): NNP = GNP − Depreciation. (निवल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद — प्रति व्यक्ति आय की गणना)

 

• NNP at factor cost, also called National Income (NI), when divided by the country's total population, gives the per capita income of the country: Per Capita Income = National Income (NNP at factor cost) ÷ Population.

 

• This makes NNP a key aggregate used in national income accounting to derive per capita income figures used for measuring a country's average standard of living.

 

• NNP essentially reflects the actual net addition to a nation's wealth, since it accounts for capital that has depreciated (worn out) during production.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The other major national income aggregates are GDP (Gross Domestic Product), GNP (Gross National Product), and NDP (Net Domestic Product), each with specific uses in economic analysis.

 

• In India, national income estimates are prepared and released by the National Statistical Office (NSO), under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

 

NOTE

 

• To calculate exports (Option 2): Exports are tracked separately via trade statistics, not derived from NNP.

 

• To calculate balance of payments (Option 3): The balance of payments is a distinct account of a country's transactions with the rest of the world, not calculated from NNP.

 

• To calculate imports (Option 4): Imports are tracked separately via trade statistics, not derived from NNP.

question: In which year did Galileo describe the regular, swinging motion of a pendulum by the action of gravity and acquired momentum?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1602.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Galileo Galilei studied the motion of pendulums and, in 1602, described in a letter to his friend Guidobaldo del Monte how a swinging pendulum moves with a regular, periodic motion under the combined action of gravity and acquired momentum (inertia). (गैलीलियो पेंडुलम — 1602)

 

• This work laid the foundation for Galileo's later, more detailed studies of isochronism — the idea that a pendulum of a given length takes approximately the same time to complete a swing regardless of the amplitude (for small oscillations).

 

• Galileo is said to have first noticed this property of pendulums while observing a swinging chandelier in the Pisa Cathedral, timing its oscillations against his own pulse.

 

• His pendulum studies later influenced the development of pendulum clocks, though the first working pendulum clock was actually built by Christiaan Huygens in 1656, based partly on Galileo's principles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Galileo also made significant contributions to astronomy (improving the telescope, discovering Jupiter's four largest moons) and kinematics (studying uniformly accelerated motion using inclined planes).

 

• Galileo's pendulum-based observations are considered an early example of the scientific method, combining careful observation with quantitative measurement.

 

NOTE

 

• 1605 (Option 1): Not the year associated with Galileo's description of the pendulum's regular swinging motion.

 

• 1600 (Option 2): Not the year associated with Galileo's pendulum letter to Guidobaldo del Monte.

 

• 1599 (Option 3): Not the year associated with Galileo's pendulum letter to Guidobaldo del Monte.

question: In which year was the first Arjuna Award given to a woman hockey player?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1961.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Arjuna Award, instituted by the Government of India in 1961, is one of the country's oldest and most prestigious sports honours, recognising consistently outstanding performance in a recognised sport. (अर्जुन पुरस्कार — 1961 में स्थापना)

 

• 1961 was the very first year the Arjuna Award was conferred, and among that inaugural batch of awardees across various sporting disciplines was a woman hockey player, making 1961 the year the first Arjuna Award went to a woman hockey player.

 

• The Arjuna Award is administered by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports and, until recently, consisted of a bronze statuette of Arjuna, a certificate, ceremonial dress, and a cash prize.

 

• Field hockey has traditionally been closely linked with Indian sporting prestige, given India's dominance in the sport at the Olympic level through much of the 20th century, making early recognition of hockey players (including women) significant.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Arjuna Award is one of several national sports honours in India, alongside the higher Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award (India's highest sporting honour, renamed from Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna in 2021) and the Dronacharya Award for coaches.

 

• Major Dhyan Chand, the legendary Indian hockey player, is commemorated in the renaming of India's highest sporting award, reflecting hockey's historic stature in Indian sport.

 

NOTE

 

• 1964 (Option 1): Not the inaugural year of the Arjuna Award.

 

• 1963 (Option 2): Not the inaugural year of the Arjuna Award.

 

• 1962 (Option 3): Not the inaugural year of the Arjuna Award.
